subject: Validation engagement outline & proposed execution window — Skyline Systems
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@skylinesystems.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Validation engagement outline & proposed execution window — Skyline Systems

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. Quick recap and a concrete next-step proposal so we can line up internal owners and a target window for a short validation engagement.

High-level objective
- Validate Redwood’s inference runtime on Skyline’s summarization and routing workload (3 representative pipelines) for latency and cost at ~50k tokens/day.

Proposed execution (2-week focused validation)
1) Week 0 (this week): kickoff + access & security checklist.
   - Redwood to provide a validation playbook and deployment checklist (attached).
2) Week 1: ingest + baseline run (QA dataset) — collect latency, token cost, perf variance.
3) Week 2: split-run against Skyline traffic replay, iterate batching/quant profiles, capture SLO metrics and recommended config.

Success criteria (proposed, please edit)
- 99th percentile generation latency <= 600ms for short-turn queries (<=64 tokens).
- End-to-end cost per 1k output tokens reduced vs current baseline by >=25% (config TBD).
- No data exfiltration risk: AES-256 encrypted at rest + KMS-managed keys during test.

Owners & asks
- Redwood AE: Nikhil Sharma (manages timeline & commercial).
- Redwood SE: Lauren Bishop (test harness + config tuning).
- Skyline lead: Alex Wu (access + dataset).

Attachments: redwood-validation-playbook-v1.pdf (validation steps + runbook). I also attached a one-page template for the mutual action plan.

Timing: target kickoff Thursday 9/2 or Friday 9/3 — does that work for you?

If you want, we can also add Marissa Cole from CS to the kickoff to map post-validation rollout needs.

Thanks — will follow up once I get your preferred kickoff slot.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@skylinesystems.com>

Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@skylinesystems.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Validation engagement outline & proposed execution window — Skyline Systems

Thanks, Nikhil — that looks clear and focused. Priya and I reviewed the success criteria and propose two small tweaks before we lock dates:

1) 99th percentile latency target: we’d prefer <= 700ms for the first leg and agree to tighten to <= 600ms after tuning. Longer tail tolerated during model warm-up windows.
2) Cost: we need the cost comparison to include our existing pre-processing CDN + tokenization step so it’s apples-to-apples.

Kickoff availability: 9/3 afternoon (CT) works best for us — can we do 2pm CT / 3pm ET? We’ll provide a sanitized dataset for the baseline run (anonymized logs) and a short runbook for access.

Two asks for Redwood before kickoff:
- A short SOC/PCI pointer doc and the exact KMS flow you use for private deployments (Priya will validate with InfoSec).
- A blank MOU we can review (we have procurement windows next week).

We’re excited to get this going; if we see the cost/latency lift we’ll look to expand to two more pipelines in Q4.

—Alex
Alex Wu
Head of ML Engineering | Skyline Systems
alex.wu@skylinesystems.com
+1 (312) 555-6789

Perfect — shared the sanitized dataset (Drive link: https://drive.google.com/example/sanitized-dataset) and a short doc describing the three pipelines:
- Summarization (customer support transcripts) — ~avg 120 tokens out; short-turn queries ~<64 tokens.
- Routing (intent classifier + prompt routing) — bursty pattern, important tail latency.
- Document enrichment (embedding + retrieval step) — longer sequences, stress test KV cache.

Priya got the MOU and will route it to procurement; she asked for a target billing estimate for the 2-week run so procurement has a budget anchor. If you can provide a ballpark (not final) that would help speed approval.

Final note: InfoSec asked for the SOC pointer doc and a brief KMS sentence on how keys are scoped (customer key, rotation cadence) — that should be enough for an initial gating review.

Looking forward to kickoff on 9/3 3pm ET.

Thanks,
Alex
